THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Harman, Isaac” (poll_1834_050, line 219). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Harman' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Isaac' is identical and the surnames differ by one interior vowel. Isaac Dewey Harmon is documented and anchored — Fergus's old-settler notice of 9 April 1886, the 1833 tax list, the Black Hawk muster of 1832, the Democrat of 17 December 1833 and 5 August 1835 — and the `harmon-isaac` cluster has already folded a bare 'Isaac Harmon' onto him under C3 as the one Isaac Harmon the town documents. An 'Isaac Harman' on the 1834 poll looks like the same man with the vowel mis-set.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE ROLL THAT SETS HARMAN SETS HARMON ON THE NEXT TWO LINES, FOR OTHER MEN. The poll filed 11 August 1834 enters 'Harman, Isaac' at voter_lists_1833_1835.txt line 219 and then 'Harmon, C. L.' at 220 and 'Harmon, M. D.' at 221 — one roll, one clerk, both spellings, deliberately distinguished within three lines. That is the opposite of C9's demonstration: the printing is caught keeping the spellings apart. Isaac Dewey Harmon's own readings are on the 1833 tax list and not on that poll, so no roll sets both spellings for HIM; and the Harmon stem is heavily populated here — harmon_charles_l, harmon_d, harmon_elijah_d, harmon_isaac_d, harmon_m_d, five cards — while Harman has one. D9, and the C3 fold inside the `harmon-isaac` cluster is untouched because it folded a card spelled Harmon.
